title: Transcriptomic effects of lead on the differentiation of human embryonic stem cells into ectoderm: implication for adverse pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: Epidemiological studies revealed associations between maternal lead (Pb) exposure and adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes as well as neurodevelopmental disorders. However, the underlying mechanisms remained unclear, and thus was investigated at the transcriptional level in this study using human embryonic stem cells (hESCs). Differentiation of hESCs to ectoderm was induced for 7 days using STEMdiff™ Trilineage Differentiation Kit containing 0 (water), 6.2 (geometric mean concentration of Pb in human maternal blood), or 118 µg Pb2+/L, in the form of lead chloride (PbCl2), followed by bulk RNA sequencing. Both doses of PbCl2 altered gene expression related to protein metabolism and trafficking, while also causing changes in genes involved in gastrulation, proliferation, DNA repair, stress response, and immune-cell development. PbCl2 at the low dose induced gene changes predicting decreased cell proliferation and increased sensory loss. Cells exposed to the high dose of PbCl2 had a distinct global gene expression profile from that of control cells with specific changes predicting increased neurodegeneration. The differences in expression of ectoderm lineage marker genes (ELMG) between control and PbCl2 treated cells did not reach statistical significance. However, expression of some genes downstream of ELMG differed markedly between control and PbCl2 treated cells. Multiple adverse outcome pathways involving WNT, IGF-1, RHO-PKN, CDK5, MAP kinase, and Ca2+ signaling, cell cycle control, protein metabolism and trafficking, DNA double strand break and repair, and immune response were detected in PbCl2 treated cells. Overall, the findings suggest that Pb exposure disrupted early ectodermal development by prioritizing genome preservation over fate execution.

title: KCNQ1 disruption alters human neuronal development through mitochondrial and insulin signalling pathways.
abstract: KCNQ1 encodes a voltage-gated potassium channel implicated in peripheral and neurological disorders, but its role in human neurodevelopment remains unclear. We generated KCNQ1 knockout (KO) human induced pluripotent stem cells and differentiated them into neural stem cells (NSCs) and cortical neurons. KCNQ1-deficient NSCs show impaired neurite outgrowth, linked to reduced cell adhesion and disrupted neural cell adhesion molecule signalling, a phenotype reproduced by pharmacological KCNQ1 inhibition. Multi-omics and follow-up analyses reveal mitochondrial dysfunction, including reduced mitochondrial copy number and ATP synthase expression. KO cells also show impaired insulin signalling, with diminished insulin receptor gene expression and altered RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT pathways. In differentiated neuronal cultures, KCNQ1 loss decreases synaptic activity and maintains an immature transcriptional profile. Together, these findings identify a role for KCNQ1 in regulating cell adhesion, mitochondrial function, insulin signalling, and neuronal maturation, expanding our understanding of processes that may contribute to neurological manifestations associated with KCNQ1-related disorders.

title: Perspectives on ionizing radiation and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Emerging evidence from terrestrial cohorts suggests that ionizing radiation (IR) exposure may increase the risk of Parkinson's disease (PD). Understanding the biological mechanisms underlying IR-induced PD is therefore critical for assessing health risks, particularly in the context of long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars. This perspective explores mechanistic pathways that may support causal links between IR and PD and highlights experimental and epidemiological approaches relevant for strengthening causal inference.

title: Author Correction: Engineered CRISPR-OsCas12f1 and RhCas12f1 with robust activities and expanded target range for genome editing.
Huntington's disease vasculopathy is barrier-type-selective and arteriolar-dominant with spatially-coupled astrogliosis and reversible by S1pr1 stimulation.
abstract: Brain vascular barriers are dysfunctional in many neurological disorders, including Huntington's disease (HD), but which vessels are affected and how remains unclear. Using in vivo two-photon microscopy in R6/2 HD-model mice, we reveal a striking divergence in barrier dysfunction. Surface vessels of the blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier (BCSFB) drive pathology in HD by paracellular leakage, while parenchymal vessels forming the blood-brain barrier (BBB) exhibit increased vesicular transport and adsorptive-mediated transcytosis (AMT), with arterioles representing the most critically impacted vascular segment. The pathology of both barriers was spatially-matched with astrocyte activation pattern localized to affected vessels both in R6/2 mice and in brains of HD patients. Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1pr1) agonist treatment reversed BCSFB leakage and partially restored BBB function, selectively reducing AMT in arterioles, with no effect in capillaries and venules. These findings redefine HD vascular pathology, demonstrating heterogeneous, vessel-type-specific barrier failure beyond generalized "disruption," uncovering mechanistic vulnerabilities and the therapeutic potential of S1pr1 modulation.

title: Single-cell, spatial, and machine learning analyses identify ANKIB1 as an oligodendrocyte-anchored palmitoylation-associated candidate biomarker of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline, yet most candidate therapies targeting amyloid-β have failed to robustly modify disease progression, underscoring an incomplete mechanistic understanding. Oligodendrocytes (ODCs) have recently emerged as active contributors to AD pathology, but the cell-type-specific role of protein S-palmitoylation - a reversible lipid post-translational modification regulating membrane targeting and trafficking - in AD remains uncharacterized. Here we performed an integrated multi-omics analysis combining single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE233208; 48,714 cells), five bulk transcriptomic cohorts (769 samples), and 10× Visium spatial transcriptomic data from 16 brain sections. Palmitoylation activity was quantified at single-cell resolution using a curated 46-gene set; machine learning frameworks (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were used to distil a parsimonious biomarker panel; and four complementary metrics (Jaccard index, overlap coefficient, colocalization percentage, and odds ratio) were applied to evaluate spatial gene-cell colocalization. Oligodendrocytes emerged as the cell population most strongly enriched for palmitoylation activity in the AD brain, supported by per-cell-type scoring, odds ratio enrichment, and an ODC-anchored 658-gene palmitoylation module. Intersection with AD-associated differentially expressed genes yielded 89 candidate genes, from which machine learning identified a seven-gene biomarker panel (ANKIB1, SPAG9, HBP1, SLC25A29, FAM171A1, ATXN10, and NDUFV1). ANKIB1 consistently topped every layer of analysis, with the highest AUC for AD discrimination (0.813, 95% CI 0.782-0.844) and persistent spatial colocalization with ODC-enriched regions across early AD and AD. Network pharmacology nominated AHR and TRIM11 as candidate upstream regulators and catalogued compounds with reported gene interactions. These findings identify the ODC-palmitoylation axis as a previously underappreciated dimension of AD biology and position ANKIB1 as a leading candidate biomarker of ODC dysfunction in AD.

title: Loss of oxytocin receptor function disrupts neural signatures of pair bonding and fidelity in the nucleus accumbens.
abstract: Enduring relationships dramatically shape behaviors by promoting affiliation between familiar individuals; however, the neural mechanisms driving attachments remain unclear. Oxytocin receptor (Oxtr) signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) reinforces pair bond formation in socially monogamous prairie voles. How Oxtr influences NAc activity during affiliative behaviors with partners and rejection of strangers is unknown. Using in vivo fiber photometry, we demonstrate that genetic loss of Oxtr sex-specifically disrupts attachment behaviors and associated NAc activity. In females, loss of Oxtr reduces prosocial behaviors and NAc activity during initial chemosensory investigation of novel males; however, partner-directed affiliative behavior and associated activity increase independently of Oxtr. In males, loss of Oxtr increases prosocial investigation of novel females, and initial behavioral and neural activity patterns predict future partner preference in Oxtr-null males. These findings reveal sex-specific roles for Oxtr in early pair bond development through modulation of prosociality and sensory processing.

title: Perinatal maternal distress and neurobehavioural development in toddlers.
abstract: Maternal perinatal psychological distress (e.g., anxiety, depression) is common and has been linked to adverse child behavioural outcomes. Altered brain function provides a potential mechanism through which perinatal distress may impact child behaviour, but specific associations remain unclear. This study investigated associations between perinatal distress, child brain functional connectivity at 2 years, and child behaviour at 2 and 3 years. Neuroimaging and behavioural data were obtained from the Pregnancy during the COVID-19 Pandemic (PdP) study. Maternal distress (anxiety and depression symptoms) was self-reported throughout the perinatal period; analyses included measures from intake survey and 2 years postpartum. Child behaviour at 2 and 3 years was parent-reported using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ-3). Resting-state fMRI data was collected at 2 years (n = 62) to quantify connectivity within the default mode, executive control, frontoparietal, and sensorimotor networks. Associations between maternal prenatal and postnatal distress, child functional connectivity, and child behaviour were examined using regression models. Postnatal, but not prenatal, distress was associated with lower gross motor scores at 2 years (B = -0.5, T = -2.8, p = 0.005, df = 3517, q = 0.01). Higher distress both prenatally and postnatally was associated with lower ASQ-3 scores at 3 years across all domains (q < 0.05). Child brain connectivity was not related to maternal distress or behaviour. Perinatal distress was associated with worse behaviour at 2 and 3 years, although no associations with connectivity were observed, suggesting other pathways may underlie these effects. Nonetheless, these findings highlight the importance of supporting mental health during pregnancy and postnatally to promote healthy child development.

title: Sphingolipid and ceramide associations with tau pathology vary across diverse ethnoracial groups in postmortem brain tissue.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Metabolic dysregulation is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD), with numerous studies characterizing metabolic pathways associated with AD onset and progression. A limitation of these studies has been a focus on non-Hispanic white participants. Despite evidence that AD prevalence, progression, and biomarkers differ across ethnoracial groups, it remains unclear whether previously identified metabolic dysregulation in AD brains generalizes across populations. We analyzed metabolomics data from 547 postmortem brain tissue samples of Hispanic American, Non-Hispanic African American, and White subjects, providing the largest multiethnic AD brain cohort to date. A metabolome-wide association study examined how relationships between metabolite abundance and AD neuropathology varied by ethnoracial group. Forty-eight metabolites exhibited significant heterogeneity with tau pathology (Braak stage), with enrichment in tricarboxylic-acid-cycle intermediates and sphingolipid-ceramide pathway lipids, and with metabolite-tau associations driven predominantly by the Hispanic American and non-Hispanic White groups. These findings reveal ethnoracial-specific metabolic signatures of tau pathology and emphasize the need to evaluate emerging therapeutic targets across diverse groups.

title: Brain microstructure mediates the relationship between Alzheimer's proteinopathies and memory.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: We examined how amyloid beta (Aβ) and tau accumulation affected gray matter (GM) microstructural integrity and how such alterations impacted memory. We tested voxel-wise mediation models to examine the relationships between (1) positron emission tomography-derived Aβ and tau accumulation and GM microstructural integrity assessed with neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, (2) GM microstructural integrity and memory controlling for Aβ and tau, and (3) the indirect effect of Aβ and tau on memory through GM microstructural integrity in 194 participants with memory impairments. Tau had a greater impact on GM microstructure than did Aβ. GM microstructural alterations in posterior cortical regions were associated with worse memory when controlling for Alzheimer's proteinopathies. GM microstructural alterations mediated the relationship between Alzheimer's proteinopathies and memory. GM microstructural alterations have functional ramifications given their mediating effect on the relationship between Alzheimer's proteinopathies and memory and their association with worse memory beyond Alzheimer's proteinopathies.

title: Sex-specific brain reserve and progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease dementia.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Sex differences exist in Alzheimer's disease (AD) treatment response, but the role of sex in disease development and progression remains unclear. We performed multimodal analyses of AD biomarker-positive individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI; MCI n = 593, AD n = 270) and National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (MCI n = 436, AD n = 174). Baseline gray matter volume (GMV) was compared by sex. In ADNI, tau positron emission tomography burden and cerebrospinal fluid growth-associated protein 43 (GAP-43) were assessed. Longitudinal analyses examined atrophy and conversion from MCI to dementia. Females with MCI exhibited greater baseline GMV than males primarily in the thalamus, caudate, cerebellum, postcentral gyrus, and middle cingulate gyrus, with no differences at the AD stage. Despite this, females exhibited higher baseline GAP-43, greater tau burden in temporal and parietal regions, and more rapid annual hippocampal atrophy. Conversion rates were similar. Findings suggest that females may tolerate greater pathology at early stages but experience faster neurodegeneration later, supporting sex-specific disease trajectories and highlighting the need for sex-informed biomarkers.

title: [Mechanism of Danhong Injection in regulating endometrial breakdown during menstruation via HIF1A/CXCR4 pathway].
journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the effects of Danhong Injection on endometrial breakdown in a menstrual-like mouse model and its underlying mechanisms.In this study,a menstrual-like mouse model was established,and uterine tissue morphology was observed at different time points after progesterone(P4) withdrawal.The menstrual-like mice were randomly divided into a sham group,a model group,low-(0.6 mL·kg~(-1)) and high-(1.2 mL·kg~(-1)) dose Danhong Injection groups,and a high-dose Danhong Injection plus hypoxia-inducible factor-lα(HIF1A) inhibitor(PX-478,40 mg·kg~(-1)) group.The results show that 24 hours after P4withdrawal,compared with those in the sham group,the mice in the model group exhibit decreased serum P4 and estradiol(E_2)levels,increased follicle-stimulating hormone(FSH) and luteinizing hormone(LH) levels,endometrial breakdown,and significantly increased apoptosis rate.The gene and protein expression of inflammatory cytokines,such as tumor necrosis factor-α(TNF-α),interleukin-6(IL-6),interleukin-10(IL-10),and cluster of differentiation 45(CD45) were increased.The gene and protein expression of apoptosis-related proteins,such as activated cleaved caspase-3,HIF1A,and C-X-C chemokine receptor 4(CXCR4),were also increased.The B-cell lymphoma-2(Bcl-2)/Bcl-2-associated X protein(Bax) decreased.After Danhong Injection intervention,especially in the high-dose Danhong Injection group,serum P4 levels were increased,while E_2,FSH,and LH levels were decreased.Endometrial breakdown and apoptosis were alleviated;inflammatory cytokines and cleaved caspase-3 expression were downregulated;IL-10 levels,Bcl-2/Bax,and gene and protein expression of HIF1A and CXCR4 were unregulated.By 48 hours after P4 withdrawal,partial endometrial repair occurred in the mice from the model group,with increased protein expression of α-smooth muscle actin(α-SMA) and matrix metalloproteinase-9(MMP-9),while mRNA expression of HIF1A and CXCR4 showed no significant changes.Although Danhong Injection with different doses did not significantly alter serum hormone levels at this time point,it accelerated endometrial repair and reduced α-SMA and MMP-9 protein expression.The HIF1A inhibitor PX-478 reversed its positive effects during the repair phase.In summary,Danhong Injection may delay P4 withdrawal and improve the hormonal environment,thereby alleviating endometrial breakdown in menstrual-like mice.In the local endometrium,its mechanism of action may be related to activating the HIF1A/CXCR4 signaling pathway,inhibiting excessive stromal cell apoptosis,alleviating inflammatory responses,and promoting tissue homeostasis restoration.

title: Multidisciplinary perspectives on managing functional/dissociative seizures in the emergency department: A survey of medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians.
abstract: Patients with functional/dissociative seizures (FDS) commonly present to emergency departments (ED), but the practices of the multidisciplinary emergency care workforce have not been described. A cross-sectional survey was administered to medical, nursing, and allied health clinicians at two EDs of an Australian metropolitan tertiary health service, between August-December 2025. Closed items were analysed descriptively; open-ended responses were analysed using conventional qualitative content analysis. Of 930 clinicians invited, 101 participated (55 medical, 36 nursing, 10 allied health); 93 (92%) had witnessed a FDS in their ED work, yet 88 (87%) reported little to no training and 73 (72%) had little to no understanding of FDS. Management approaches employed included reassurance (49%), a safe low-stimulus environment (28%) and watchful waiting (29%), with deliberately conservative pharmacology amongst more experienced medical staff. Challenges included treatment disagreement (30%), patient or family expectations (30%) and stigma (21%). Three priorities emerged: a departmental pathway (32%), patient-specific management plans (18%), and multidisciplinary training (18%). Multidisciplinary emergency care clinicians manage FDS based on clinical experience rather than formal training. The three priorities identified by ED clinicians for practice development require prospective evaluation.

title: The ever-expanding universe of botulinum neurotoxin in movement disorders.
abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) has become a cornerstone in the management of movement disorders since its introduction into neurological practice. Initially established as a first-line therapy for focal dystonias and other hyperkinetic conditions, its efficacy is supported by robust clinical evidence and guideline recommendations. BoNT exerts its therapeutic effects through inhibition of acetylcholine release via cleavage of SNARE proteins, resulting in reversible chemodenervation, with additional evidence supporting modulation of sensory pathways and central motor circuits. This present review intends to summarize the clinical use of BoNT beyond established ones in dystonia and spasticity, as expanding applications accrue. The expanse includes treatment of Parkinson and Non-Parkinson-related movement disorders, hyperexcitability syndromes, autonomic blockade and pain reduction. Emerging utility of BoNT clinical use include the applications at Intensive Care Unit, the pre-emptive use of BoNT during surgeries and the device aided BoNT deliveries. These developments highlight its evolving role as a versatile therapy beyond purely motor control. Despite growing clinical experience, many emerging indications remain supported by limited or heterogeneous evidence. Further studies are needed to define optimal patient selection, dosing strategies, and long-term outcomes. As understanding of disease mechanisms continues to evolve, BoNT is poised to remain at the forefront of personalized and precision-based therapies in movement disorders.

title: The divergent 3D genome landscapes of aging and neurodegenerative mouse models.
abstract: Chromatin structure is essential for gene regulation and genome stability, as neurons must preserve their 3D genome organization throughout life. This structure gradually deteriorates with aging and is further disrupted in neurodegenerative diseases. To investigate whether aging and neurodegeneration share early chromatin changes or diverge, we perform Hi-C on cortical neurons from adult, aged, and brain-specific SIRT6-knockout (S6-KO) mice and compare them to the previously published Hi-C data sets from a CK-p25 Alzheimer's disease model stratified by γH2AX levels. All models show early features such as weakened interactions between chromosomes in expanded nuclei, A- to B-compartment shifts, and loss of architectural loops. However, aged neurons retain TAD prominence, short-range interactions, and enhancer-promoter loops, whereas pathological models showed reduced TAD prominence, shorter loops, and disorganized A-B mixing. These changes correlate with increased DNA damage. Our findings suggest that aging represents a "primed" state, in which chromatin regulation begins to erode, but further stressors like DNA damage are associated with progression toward neurodegenerative breakdown.

title: Altered Brain Extracellular Matrix Structure and Sex-Specific Learning/Memory Dysfunction in Mice Lacking the Functional Amyloid Cystatin-Related Epididymal Spermatogenic (CRES).
abstract: The brain's extracellular matrix (ECM) is highly specialized and unique. Unlike the collagen-rich matrices found in other tissues, it consists of complex proteoglycans and glycosaminoglycans that play critical roles in neuroplasticity including the integration and storage of new memories. Cystatin-related epididymal spermatogenic (CRES) is a member of a reproductive subgroup of family 2 cystatins and part of a specialized functional amyloid-containing ECM with host defense functions in the epididymal lumen. CRES and the endogenous epididymal amyloid matrix exhibit high plasticity, forming distinct amyloid structures, with antimicrobial functions tailored to specific bacterial strains. Recent studies show that CRES/CRES amyloid is also present in the mammalian brain ECM and suggest its inherent shape-shifting properties might contribute to neuroplasticity. In this study, we utilized a CRES knockout (KO) mouse model to determine if the loss of CRES altered the structure of the hippocampal and cortical ECM and impacted brain function. We report that CRES KO male and female mice exhibited sex-specific structural changes in both the loose/interstitial and perineuronal net (PNN) ECM. Additionally, young CRES KO males-but not females-displayed deficits in learning, memory and executive functioning when compared to WT controls. In contrast, older CRES KO males did not exhibit behavioral deficits, a finding that correlated with the observation of a similar PNN ECM structure when compared to WT mice. Our data suggest that CRES functions as a regulatory or structural component of the brain ECM, contributing to its sex-specific structural organization and plasticity, affecting sex-specific behaviors of learning and memory.Significance statement Structural changes in the brain ECM drive neuroplasticity that is essential for normal function; however, these same alterations can contribute to neurodegeneration and neurological disorders. Brain ECM structure differs between males and females and promotes sex-specific behaviors; however, the full extent of sex-specific distinctions in ECM structure/function relationships has yet to be elucidated. Using a CRES KO mouse model, we show that the functional amyloid CRES plays a regulatory/structural role in the brain ECM. The loss of CRES resulted in sex differences in loose/interstitial and PNN ECM organization and a male but not female learning and memory deficit. Our studies suggest that CRES/CRES amyloid contributes to ECM neuroplasticity and remodeling processes that drive sex-specific behaviors and possibly sexually dimorphic disease.

title: Generalized Linear Mixed Models for Changepoint Analysis of Biomedical Time Series Data.
abstract: Changepoint analysis for time series data identifies the time points for which properties about the data shift. In this paper, we are motivated by two distinct types of biomedical time series data: digital health monitoring and neuroimaging. The neuroimaging study consists of multivariate time series obtained from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). The digital health monitoring data consists of binary univariate time series observed within an individual throughout the day across multiple days of activity. The goal of the analysis is to model how physical activity changes within a day over a period of 56 days. The goal in the analysis of that data is to determine the association between dynamic functional connectivity (dFC), which is the interaction between different brain regions and how this interaction changes over time, and severity of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI). In this paper, we leverage the framework of generalized linear mixed models to incorporate structure that is present in biomedical time series data for changepoint analysis. This structure could be, for example, the repeated measures of the time series data within an individual across multiple days or the interconnected community structure of brain networks. We embed the mixed model in a dynamic programming algorithm for detecting multiple changepoints. We evaluate the performance of our proposed method across several scenarios using simulations. Finally, we show the utility of our proposed method on our two distinct motivating applications.

Vestibular Event Monitoring in the Community and Emergency Room.
abstract: Patients who are experiencing an attack of acute vertigo often demonstrate nystagmus that could provide useful diagnostic clues that identify the underlying vestibular disorder. Such ictal nystagmus is encountered in primary care, emergency rooms and patients' home environments where methods of recording nystagmus (video nystagmography) are scarce. Investigators worldwide have endeavored to circumvent this difficulty by using novel service models or portable nystagmus recording devices. Here we describe the event-monitoring techniques used thus far and summarize the diagnostic information gathered by ictal video nystagmography.

title: Clinical Assessment of Otolith-Ocular Function: A Practical Guide and Review of the Video-Ocular Counter-Roll.
abstract: Otolith organs play a central role in gaze stabilization, spatial orientation, and postural control. Advances in video-oculography have created new opportunities to assess this key aspect of vestibular function directly at the bedside. Using this technology, the video ocular counter-roll (vOCR) test extends vestibular evaluation to the otolith-ocular system by measuring ocular counter-roll (OCR), a torsional vestibulo-ocular response during lateral head tilt. This review provides a practical guide to the clinical application of vOCR, including setup, analysis, and interpretation, and discusses its diagnostic utility for assessing otolith-ocular function, characterizing patterns of vestibular loss, and monitoring recovery.

title: Multimodal artificial intelligence to predict cardiomyopathy development in hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis.
Switch costs reveal vocal-specific executive demands during flexible action selection in crows.
abstract: Crows and other corvids exhibit remarkable cognitive flexibility, exercising volitional control that allows them to select, initiate and withhold actions based on deliberate decisions rather than reflex. Among these behaviours, vocalizations are especially demanding, yet crows perform them with exceptional precision, paralleling core building blocks of human speech. Despite this, the executive mechanisms supporting intentional vocal control, and how they differ from those governing other voluntary actions, remain largely unknown. We trained carrion crows to produce either vocalizations or pecking responses to arbitrary visual cues presented in randomized, alternating or blocked sequences that controlled how often response modalities switched across trials. While crows performed both actions with high accuracy, vocalizations were consistently slower and more variable than pecking. Notably, vocalizations showed clear switch costs; transitions into vocal responses caused slower reaction times and occasional errors, whereas pecking was largely unaffected. These results show that crows can flexibly switch between motor modalities and that volitional vocalizations carry specific cognitive control demands, previously undescribed in birds. Crows thus stand out as a rare non-primate species in which volitional vocalizations integrate speed, accuracy and executive control.

title: Self-organized spectral adjustment in echolocation sounds within group-flying bats.
abstract: Self-organized behaviour has been extensively studied in group dynamics in animals, with a strong focus on movement coordination in species like fish and birds. By contrast, far less attention has been paid to vocal interactions within animal groups. Here, we unveil a self-organized vocal behaviour in echolocating bats (Miniopterus fuliginosus), characterized by their adaptive responses to jamming stimuli. Using controlled playback experiments, we identified a mathematical model that describes how bats autonomously adjust their vocal frequencies to avoid signal interference mimicking group echolocation. The model was subsequently extended to simulate a group of bats flying in two-dimensional space. Consistent with previous observations of group-flying bats, the simulation revealed frequency-adjusting behaviour, characterized by an overall increase in frequency differences within the group. Crucially, we demonstrated that this behaviour reduces potential misdetections during echolocation, enhancing group-wide sensory accuracy. These results reveal a mechanism of conflict resolution through self-organized vocal adjustment and establish a parallel with other self-organizing systems in nature. Our findings reveal that this frequency-adjusting behaviour represents a self-organized vocal behaviour that effectively mitigates conflicts within a group, one achieved via simple behavioural rules, as in other types of collective animal behaviour.

title: Microbiome-mediated resilience and cross-generational consequences in male Drosophila exposed to combined environmental stressors.
abstract: Climate change exposes organisms to multiple, interacting stressors, yet their joint effects on reproduction and inheritance remain poorly understood. This study investigated the interactive effects of acute heat stress and sublethal imidacloprid exposure on the reproductive success of male Drosophila melanogaster and the subsequent fitness of their offspring. We manipulated the gut microbiome of male flies (germ-free or colonized with one or five bacterial species) and subjected them to individual or combined stress. We show that combined stressors act synergistically to reduce male fitness traits, an effect that is partially buffered by higher microbiome diversity. Paternal stress exposure further reduced offspring fertility, demonstrating cross-generational fitness costs largely independent of microbial transmission. Our results underscore the gut microbiome as an important, but stress-sensitive, contributor to host resilience, and demonstrate how multi-stressor interactions can amplify reproductive failure, with broad implications for population persistence and biodiversity loss in a warming, chemically altered world.

title: Lighting and circadian cues shape locomotor strategies for balance and navigation in larval zebrafish.
abstract: Most fish are inherently unstable and must swim to stabilize posture. How diurnal fish reduce activity at night while maintaining postural control remains unclear. We defined distinct locomotor strategies that larval zebrafish (Danio rerio) use to control posture and navigate the water column in response to light and circadian cues. In the dark, larvae maintain balance by swimming in long bouts with large nose-up rotations, compensating for nose-down drift accrued during prolonged inactivity. Effective postural compensation requires vestibular sensation from the utricle. By contrast, in the light, larvae navigate with short, frequent and variable bouts. While lighting exerts a dominant, masking effect on the locomotor strategies, circadian rhythms modulate swim kinematics. Our results reveal distinct light-dark locomotor strategies and disentangle how ambient light and the internal clock jointly shape balance control and navigation. This work lays the foundation for understanding how external and internal cues interact to govern locomotor activity in freely moving diurnal animals.

title: Ear-Worn Inertial Measurement of Sit-to-Stand and Sit-to-Walk Movements: Algorithm Development and Validation.
abstract: Sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk are common functional movements that provide insight into an individual's functional mobility. Developing comprehensive measures of these movements using ear-worn inertial measurement units (IMUs), which are increasingly incorporated into widely used devices such as hearing aids and headphones, could provide a means of monitoring older adults and individuals with movement disorders with minimal additional burden. This paper aimed to introduce comprehensive outcome measures for sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk movements based on data from ear-worn IMUs, and to evaluate their agreement with an optical motion capture reference. Data were analyzed from 62 participants, of whom 46 (18 male and 28 female; median age 27, IQR 15 years) did not have a known underlying movement condition and 16 (7 male and 9 female; median age 62, IQR 23 years) did. The participants wore a bespoke 3D-printed headset that contained 6-axis IMUs placed beside their left and right ears. A reflective marker was placed on each participant's seventh cervical vertebra to provide an optical motion capture reference. Each participant performed 3 sit-to-stand movements and 3 sit-to-walk movements. The reported outcome metrics included overall and subphase durations, acceleration, velocity, power, movement smoothness, and hesitation. Agreement between ear-derived and optical outcomes was evaluated using linear mixed-effects analyses accounting for repeated trials within participants, including systematic and proportional bias, limits of agreement, root mean squared error, and smallest detectable difference. Temporal outcomes demonstrated the closest agreement between systems. The mean overall movement duration differed by 0.09 (SD 0.12) seconds for sit-to-stand and 0.06 (SD 0.17) seconds for sit-to-walk, with 95% limits of agreement of -0.14 to 0.32 seconds and -0.28 to 0.39 seconds, respectively. Strong linear relationships were observed for peak power, with mixed-effects regression slopes of 0.70 for sit-to-stand and 0.68 for sit-to-walk, although systematic biases of 172 (95% CI 153-190) W and 191 (95% CI 168-215) W indicated that ear-derived and seventh cervical vertebra-derived power were not interchangeable. Peak upward acceleration similarly showed systematic biases of 1.05 (95% CI 0.93-1.18) and 1.30 ms-2 (95% CI 1.14-1.45) for sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk, respectively. Hesitation demonstrated comparatively small absolute error (root mean squared error 0.04 and 0.03, respectively), whereas smoothness and other fluency outcomes showed greater disagreement between measurement systems. The ear-worn IMUs extracted a broad range of sit-to-stand and sit-to-walk outcome measures, although agreement with the optical reference varied between measures. Temporal outcomes demonstrated the closest agreement, whereas kinematic, power, and fluency measures showed varying degrees of systematic and proportional disagreement. These findings support the feasibility of using ear-worn IMUs for comprehensive functional movement assessment and provide a basis for subsequent validation of the most robust outcomes in clinically relevant populations.

title: Mechanistic advances in exercise intervention for anxiety and depression via regulation of mitochondrial function.
abstract: Anxiety and depressive disorders are the most prevalent psychiatric conditions worldwide, characterized by complex pathophysiological mechanisms involving neuroplasticity, inflammatory responses, and disturbances in energy metabolism. Mitochondrial dysfunction has been proposed as one contributor, but causal evidence in patients remains limited. Exercise is an evidence-based adjunctive option for reducing depressive and anxiety symptoms, although effect estimates vary. In this narrative review, we comprehensively summarize the current understanding of how exercise may modulate mitochondrial function, including biogenesis, dynamics and energy metabolism, and how these changes could regulate neurotransmitter systems, reduce neuroinflammation, and promote neurogenesis. By integrating findings from both preclinical and clinical studies, we assess the strength of the proposed relationship, outline requirements for causal testing, and discuss the limits of clinical translation. Furthermore, we discuss existing challenges and propose future research directions to optimize exercise-based therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial pathways for the prevention and treatment of anxiety and depressive disorders.

title: Emotional imagery alters symptom perception but not postural or respiratory behavior in individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain.
authors: Sofie Van Wesemael S V W
Ann Van Goethem A V G
abstract: Chronic non-specific low back pain (CNSLBP) often coincides with alterations in postural behavior and respiration which contribute to pain. Increasing evidence suggests that emotions are closely related to postural behavior and respiration. Thereby, emotions can affect symptom perception processes in CNSLBP. This quasi-experimental study examined how emotions affect symptom perception, postural behavior, and respiration in individuals with (n= 40) and without (n= 40) CNSLBP using script-driven emotional imagery. Participants imagined three auditory scripts describing states of relaxation, hostile-resistance, and acceptance, while standing upright on an unstable support surface with their eyes closed. During each trial, postural behavior was assessed by center of pressure (CoP) and trunk muscle electromyography (EMG), and respiration by end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂). After each trial, participants self-reported bodily complaints. Emotion-induced differences in bodily complaints, CoP, EMG, and PetCO₂ were compared between individuals with and without CNSLBP using mixed models. When compared to healthy individuals, those with CNSLBP reported more bodily complaints during the hostile-resistance (p0.05). While imagining emotional scripts did not result in alterations in postural behavior or respiration, it did alter perceived bodily complaints. This highlights the significance of symptom perception processes in individuals with CNSLBP. PERSPECTIVE: Our article provides innovative insights into the processes of symptom perception in individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain, as merely imagining an emotional script affects the perception of bodily complaints.

title: Parsing the relationships among gut microbiome, neurotransmitter metabolome, glymphatic function, and cognition across healthy elderly, mild cognitive impairment, and probable Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Evidence has suggested brain glymphatic dysfunction and gut microbial metabolic disturbance in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the relationships among gut microbiota, neurotransmitter metabolites, glymphatic function, and cognition across clinically defined groups of healthy elderly, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and probable AD remain unclear. Using metagenomic sequencing, targeted metabolomics, and multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging, we measured the gut microbiome, neurotransmitter metabolome, and a variety of glymphatic markers in 30 patients with clinically diagnosed probable AD, 75 individuals with MCI, and 59 healthy controls (HC). Although global microbial diversity showed no group difference, MCI and AD showed shared and unique species-level microbial alterations relative to HC. Despite the absence of overall metabolomic divergence, AD exhibited reduced levels of multiple neurotransmitter metabolites compared with MCI and HC. Prominent alterations in multiple glymphatic markers were present in AD rather than in MCI. Further integrated analyses revealed a wide range of associations among these multi-omics changes and established potential serial mediation pathways, manifesting as a pattern of gut microbiota → neurotransmitter metabolites → glymphatic function → cognition. These findings could enrich our understanding of the biological mechanisms involved in cognitive impairment and clinically diagnosed probable AD, but also may inform future preventive and therapeutic interventions by targeting the established pathways.

title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate esters (OPEs) and infant attention to faces at age 1 month.
abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used as flame retardants and plasticizers. Prenatal OPE exposure has been associated with adverse childhood neurodevelopment, but these outcomes are not often evaluated until well into childhood. We leveraged infants' innate preference for faces to evaluate gestational OPE exposure in relation to an early measure of cognitive processing. We measured nine mid-pregnancy urinary OPE metabolites in a U.S. UPSIDE pregnancy cohort (n=166). At age 1 month, infants were presented with a randomized series of three face-like images: standard features, scrambled features, and a featureless face shape. Using latent profile analysis, we identified three looking profiles (short, long, and selective lookers). We evaluated associations with OPE metabolites using multivariable multinomial logistic models. OPEs with >70% detection were considered continuously; less prevalent OPEs were dichotomized. Infants of mothers with detectable bis(2-methylphenyl) phosphate had greater odds of being long vs. short lookers (OR: 2.80, 95% CI: 0.99, 7.96), with stronger associations observed among females. Among boys, higher maternal dibutyl phosphate + di-isobutyl phosphate exposure was associated with 6 times the odds of being a long looker (OR: 6.05, 95%CI: 1.05, 34.92). Among girls, detectable maternal dipropyl phosphate was associated with lower odds of being a long (OR: 0.01, 95% CI: 0.001, 0.75) or a selective looker (OR <0.001, 95% CI: <0.001, 0.05). Prenatal OPE exposure may influence early face-processing, potentially in a sex-dependent manner. Follow-up is needed to assess this measure's ability to predict downstream neurodevelopmental outcomes.

title: Mitochondrial Psychobiology.
abstract: A field that uses mitochondria to unify biological and psychological sciences and to better understand the basis of health has emerged-Mitochondrial Psychobiology. Mitochondria are the body's cellular hubs for energy transformation and signaling. Mitochondria regulate functions as diverse as metabolism, gene expression, and stress adaptation; consequently, their dysregulation is linked to most chronic illnesses and aging. Here, we propose that mitochondria provide a mechanistic bridge between body and the measurable functions of the mind, including perception, cognition, emotion, and behavior. From this perspective, mitochondria provide a scientifically tractable interface through which bioenergetic processes relate to subjective experiences and behaviors. We outline foundational principles for Mitochondrial Psychobiology, discuss the key gaps that the field needs to address to advance our understanding of mind-mitochondria relationships across the lifecourse, and review emerging approaches to probe the mind-mitochondria connection across levels. This stimulating scientific challenge is a unique opportunity to train the next generation of interdisciplinary scientists, resolve conceptual and technical challenges spanning temporal and spatial scales, and develop a more accurate, holistic model of health. Rooted in general energetic principles, mitochondrial psychobiology is poised to productively steer biomedicine over the coming decades.

title: Transdiagnostic Reductions in Glymphatic-Related Perivascular Diffusion Across Psychiatric Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: The glymphatic system, a perivascular pathway supporting cerebrospinal and interstitial fluid exchange and clearance, has been implicated in neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders. Diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) provides a non-invasive proxy for glymphatic-related processes, yet its role in psychiatric conditions remains uncertain. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, PsycNET, and Embase for articles published up to September 25th, 2025. The protocol was pre-registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251155430). Studies reporting diffusion-based indices of glymphatic function in psychiatric populations were included. Standardised mean differences (Hedges' g) were calculated for patient-control comparisons and pooled using random-effects models. Heterogeneity, methodological moderators, and risk of bias were assessed. Thirty-two studies met inclusion criteria for the systematic review, covering major psychiatric groups including mood disorders, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, psychosis, sleep disorders, and substance-related conditions. Twenty-four studies (n = 2,855; 1,503 patients, 1,352 controls) reporting bilateral DTI-ALPS measures were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled random-effects model revealed a significant transdiagnostic reduction in DTI-ALPS index in psychiatric populations compared with healthy controls (Hedges' g = -0.78, 95% CI -1.01 to -0.55, p < 0.0001). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 86.3%), and there was evidence of small-study effects. Bilateral DTI-ALPS index showed a robust but heterogeneous reduction across psychiatric disorders. These results suggest that impairments of perivascular diffusion, as indexed by DTI-ALPS, may reflect a shared transdiagnostic pattern across psychiatric conditions. Harmonised imaging pipelines and multimodal validation are needed to clarify the biological and clinical significance of these findings.

title: Parallel Development and Maturation of GABAergic Interneurons and Corticotrophin-releasing Factor Signaling within the Amygdala Complex.
abstract: The amygdala complex is known to play a critical role in supporting adaptive behaviors in response to environmental stimuli, particularly during sensitive periods of brain development. Through its connections, the amygdala modulates hippocampal and striatal-dependent memories and shapes distinct cortical function within the emotional and cognitive domains. Major neural circuit remodeling is known to occur in the amygdala during postnatal development through adolescence, which includes the maturation of its excitatory connectivity and the progressive organization of local GABAergic inhibitory interneurons. Thus, the goal of this paper is to review current knowledge on how developmental trajectories of distinct GABAergic interneuron populations within the amygdala are temporally staggered to enable successive sensitive periods during which environmental input impacts amygdala-dependent emotional learning, threat processing, and social behavior. This review will discuss the early emerging somatostatin and neuropeptide Y interneurons, later maturing parvalbumin-positive interneurons, and developmental changes in stress-responsive corticotrophin-releasing factor signaling. We examine how these trajectories may shape age-appropriate behavior and sensitivity to early life adversity as GABAergic circuits within the amygdala mature.

title: TNF Receptor-2 Drives Tumoural Coagulation Factor Synthesis and Enhances Thrombosis in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most prevalent form of kidney cancer, is associated with an increased risk of local and systemic thromboembolism and a worse prognosis. The mechanisms that drive the coagulation program in tumours are not known. Combining RNAscope with immunofluorescence, local transcription of the key coagulation factors X and V, as well as prothrombin and fibrinogen chains (α, β, γ), across tumour cells, vascular endothelial cells and T cells is significantly enhanced in ccRCC tumours compared to adjacent normal kidney tissue. Elevated intratumoural protein expression of factors X and V is accompanied by local thrombin generation, fibrin deposition, and the presence of intravascular microthrombi, which themselves harbour coagulation transcripts. Mechanistic analysis using ccRCC organ cultures reveal that selective engagement of tumour necrosis factor receptor-2 (TNFR2) by a R2TNF mutein is sufficient to significantly enhance the transcription and protein expression of the same coagulation program in tumour cells, endothelial cells, and T cells compared to adjacent normal kidney cultures, whereas TNFR2 knockdown attenuates this response. In addition, TNFR2 appears to link inflammatory signalling with activation of the local coagulation system through the PI3K/Akt/MEK/NFκB signalling axes. These data provide evidence that locally produced coagulation factors driven by TNFR2 signalling may contribute to intratumoural pro-thrombotic outcomes in ccRCC, highlighting a novel pathway with potential therapeutic relevance.

title: From animal behavior to human perioperative neurocognitive disorders: translational boundaries of the gut-brain axis.
abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PND), including postoperative delirium (POD), delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR), and postoperative neurocognitive disorder, are common after surgery in older adults, and the gut-brain axis has been proposed as a contributing pathway. Most mechanistic support rests on rodent behavioral assays, yet these endpoints and human clinical diagnoses are routinely treated as interchangeable. This critical narrative review examines that translational boundary. PND is used here as a clinically consequential test case for a broader behavioral-neuroscience problem: how animal behavioral phenotypes, microbiome-associated signals, and intervention effects should be translated into human diagnostic constructs. A structured search identified and appraised the principal evidence rather than an exhaustive synthesis; no formal risk-of-bias or certainty-of-evidence assessment was performed. Evidence was separated into human perioperative studies reporting a neurocognitive outcome with either a measured gut-brain exposure or a gut-directed intervention; those reporting gut-brain change without a cognitive outcome; perioperative preclinical evidence; and indirect non-perioperative evidence. The retrieved human perioperative evidence spans observational cohorts across gastric, orthopedic, spinal and cardiac surgery, multi-omic and metabolomic cohorts, and randomized perioperative probiotic trials reporting lower rates of study-defined cognitive outcomes. It nonetheless remains heterogeneous and largely single-center, with modest event numbers, inconsistent sampling and assessment, and limited external validation. Mechanistic support still comes mainly from perioperative rodent models using water maze, fear-conditioning, recognition-memory, and delirium-like readouts, which measure narrow, species-specific capacities and are not diagnostic equivalents of POD, DNR, or postoperative neurocognitive disorder. Microbiome-mediated causation is unproven, and cross-species endpoint alignment remains a central route to improved translation.

title: Psychoneuroimmunology of Glioblastoma: How Emotional States Shape Tumor Biology.
abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

title: Pharmacological strategies for the prevention and treatment of proliferative vitreoretinopathy: A comprehensive review.
abstract: Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) represents the most significant complication and the primary cause of surgical failure in regmatogenous retinal detachment repair, occurring in approximately 5-10% of cases. The pathophysiology of PVR involves a counterproductive wound-healing response where retinal pigment epithelium and glial cells undergo dedifferentiation, migration, and proliferation. This process is largely driven by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and a complex milieu of inflammatory mediators and growth factors, most notably platelet-derived growth factor and transforming growth factor beta. We investigate the evolving role of adjuvant pharmacotherapy in preventing and treating PVR. Traditional anti-inflammatory agents and anti-vascular endothelial gowth facrtor therapies have failed to demonstrate significant improvements in anatomical reattachment rates in human clinical trials. Conversely, anti-proliferative agents have shown more clinical potential; specifically, methotrexate has emerged as a leading candidate. Other promising strategies include the use of combined 5-fluorouracil and low molecular weight heparin, daunorubicin, and emerging biological therapies such as Rho Kinase and m-TOR inhibitors. Furthermore, innovative bio-functional polymers are being developed to modulate RNA transcription and suppress EMT factors. Therefore, PVR management is shifting toward a multimodal paradigm that integrates advanced surgical techniques with targeted molecular inhibition to improve functional success.

title: mGlu7 expression is upregulated by Tcf4 deficiency in a model of Pitt Hopkins syndrome.
abstract: Pitt-Hopkins syndrome (PTHS) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder caused by de novo mutations in the Transcription Factor 4 (TCF4) gene. Clinically, phenotypes of PTHS involve motor and cognitive domains as well as epilepsy and breathing abnormalities. These phenotypes exhibit significant overlap with another disorder, Rett syndrome (RTT), caused by mutations in the Methyl-CpG-Binding Protein 2 (MECP2) gene. We have shown that expression of metabotropic glutamate receptor 7 (mGlu7) is significantly decreased in brain samples of patients with RTT, and we showed therapeutic potential of increasing mGlu7 activity in RTT model mice using a small molecule positive allosteric modulator (PAM) with mGlu7 activity. A recent study mapped TCF4 binding sites throughout the human genome and identified a TCF4 binding site in the Metabotropic Glutamate Receptor 7 (GRM7) gene. Symptom overlap, as well as the potential regulation of GRM7 by TCF4, led us to profile mGlu7 expression in the brains of Tcf4+/- animals. These studies identified an unexpected upregulation of the receptor at both the mRNA and protein level in multiple brain areas, with brain region-specific differences in the regulation of the two main mGlu7 splice variants, suggesting that these two splice variants may be distinctly regulated in the context of Tcf4 heterozygosity.

title: Prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection leads to altered neuro-immune biomarker profiles at birth.
abstract: Maternal infection during pregnancy can induce immune-mediated biological adaptations that influence fetal neurodevelopment. Although vertical transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is uncommon, the impact of maternal infection on fetal neuroimmune signaling remains poorly characterized. We investigated whether prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with alterations in circulating neuroimmune biomarkers detectable at birth. In this case-control study, 28 women with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and 61 uninfected controls were enrolled. Maternal and cord blood samples were collected at delivery. Following an initial inflammatory screening, neuro-specific biomarkers (NfL, Tau, P-Tau217, GFAP, S100β, α-Synuclein) and PTX3 were measured. Correlation network analyses, PTX3 promoter methylation assessment, and haplotype stratification analyses were also performed. Systemic inflammatory mediators did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, neonates exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection exhibited significantly lower cord blood concentrations of GFAP, NfL, and P-Tau217 and increased α-Synuclein levels compared with controls. Tau showed a decreasing trend, whereas S100β and PTX3 remained unchanged. Network analyses revealed reduced cytokine connectivity but enhanced interactions among neuro-specific biomarkers. Although PTX3 promoter methylation was unchanged, the PTX3 h2/h2 haplotype appeared to modulate biomarker interaction patterns. To our knowledge, this is the first study to characterize a circulating neuro-specific biomarker signature in neonates prenatally exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection. This supports the utility of neuroimmune biomarker networks as translational tools to investigate the biological consequences of maternal immune activation during pregnancy.

title: Editorial Perspective: The developmental exposome: timing, hierarchy, and the architecture of psychiatric risk.
journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
abstract: The psychiatric exposome offers a powerful framework for understanding how environmental conditions shape mental health across the life course, yet existing applications often reduce exposures to static, cumulative risk inventories. The exposome construct may be advanced emphasizing two interdependent dimensions: the timing of exposures within neurodevelopment and their hierarchical weight in terms of severity, chronicity, recurrence, and ecological impact. Environmental influences are neither equivalent nor context-independent, but operate through dynamic, nonlinear interactions across biological, relational, social, and cultural systems. Sensitive developmental periods, including prenatal life, infancy, childhood, and adolescence, may amplify or transform the impact of specific exposures, while protective contexts such as responsive caregiving, enriched learning environments, and prosocial peer relations can buffer risk and promote resilience. A developmentally sensitive exposome also supports transdiagnostic and preclinical approaches by identifying latent environmental dimensions that cut across categorical diagnoses. Methodological advances, including digital phenotyping, relational biomarkers, network analysis, and artificial intelligence, may enable real-time modelling of exposure trajectories. Finally, developmental exposomic clocks could be considered as clinically actionable tools to estimate environmentally driven deviations in maturation, supporting early detection, precision prevention, and individualized intervention in psychiatry across diverse clinical and community mental health settings globally.

title: Methylglyoxal exposure at dietary-relevant concentrations induces cognitive deficits through dopaminergic damage system and metabolic perturbation in zebrafish larvae.
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
abstract: This study investigated the effects of MGO exposure at dietary-relevant concentrations on cognitive function and the underlying mechanisms using zebrafish larvae. Behavioral assessments demonstrated that MGO induced dose-dependent cognitive impairment, with the medium and high dose groups showing a remarkable reduction in spatial memory and locomotor activity. Mechanistic investigations revealed that MGO triggered substantial oxidative stress, evidenced by suppressed antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD and CAT decreased by approximately 30% and 28%, respectively, in the high-dose group) and elevated lipid peroxidation (MDA increased by 3.5-fold). These changes were accompanied by dopaminergic system impairment, including neurotransmitter depletion (dopamine levels reduced to 0.27±0.01 μg/g prot in high dose group) and neuronal degeneration (neuronal density decreased by 39%). Metabolomics analysis identified 37 differential metabolites across all groups, with significant enrichment in glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways. Our findings establish a comprehensive mechanistic pathway linking MGO exposure to cognitive deficits through oxidative stress-mediated dopaminergic damage and metabolic dysregulation, suggesting potential neurotoxic risks of dietary carbonyl compounds and underscoring the need for further mechanistic and translational studies. This study provides a preliminary toxicological basis for food safety evaluation, while acknowledging that validation in higher vertebrate systems is essential for human risk assessment.

title: D2 dopamine and CB2 cannabinoid receptor cooperation restores striatal LTP in an epilepsy model.
abstract: Increasing evidence suggests that subcortical structures contribute to seizure susceptibility and cognitive impairment in several epileptic syndromes. However, research into mechanisms linking neuronal excitability and synaptic dysfunction in epilepsy has mainly focused on the cortex and hippocampus, leaving basal ganglia contributions largely unexplored. Using a genetic murine model of Lafora disease (LD), a drug-resistant form of neurodegenerative epilepsy, we performed ex vivo patch-clamp recordings to assess neuronal excitability, synaptic transmission, and plasticity of striatal medium spiny neurons. Our results reveal progressive alterations in corticostriatal transmission and long-term synaptic plasticity, including long-term potentiation (LTP). Electrophysiological and biochemical assessments showed a reduced NMDA/AMPA ratio and reduced expression of NMDA receptor subunits and dopamine receptors in striatal neurons of LD mice. Exposure to a dopamine D2 receptor agonist and to cannabidiol restored long-term plasticity in LD mice, suggesting a D2R- and CB2R-dependent synergic action on striatal LTP. Our findings highlight basal ganglia dysfunction in experimental epilepsy and suggest an unconventional dopaminergic-endocannabinoid interplay.

title: Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody reveals a novel strategy for understanding and treating early-onset neuromuscular diseases.
abstract: Congenital myasthenia (CM) comprises a group of neuromuscular diseases caused by mutations in genes responsible for the formation and function of neuromuscular synapses, including genes encoding neuronal Agrin, low-density receptor-related protein 4 (Lrp4), muscle-specific kinase (MuSK), downstream of kinase 7 (Dok7), and receptor-associated protein (Rapsyn). Although mouse models have been invaluable for studying neuromuscular diseases, including CM, early neonatal lethality, due to respiratory failure, has made it difficult to study disease progression or assess potential treatments. Previously, we demonstrated that postnatal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody rescued neuromuscular synapses and prevented disease in a mouse model of Dok7 CM. To determine whether a MuSK agonist antibody could benefit other forms of CM, we delivered a MuSK agonist antibody to pregnant mice and thereby their progeny. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody prevented neonatal lethality of Dok7 mutant mice, allowing the mice to survive for at least two months. Maternal delivery of a MuSK agonist antibody also rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice from neonatal lethality, but the mice failed to survive for two months, even after additional postnatal treatment with the agonist antibody. Partial and full denervation were prominent in rescued neuronal agrin mutant mice, suggesting that poor attachment and withdrawal of nerve terminals are responsible for their postnatal lethality. These findings indicate that neuronal Agrin has functions in synaptic differentiation and maintenance that are independent of MuSK activation. Classifications: Biological Sciences / Neuroscience.

title: Dietary heme iron intake and common hemochromatosis HFE polymorphisms have similar associations with brain MRI phenotypes: a UK Biobank cohort study.
abstract: Brain iron accumulation is associated with aging and neurodegeneration, but how individual genetics and dietary iron intake affect brain iron is not well understood. Hemochromatosis is a genetic disorder arising from single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the HFE gene, causing iron overload and brain iron accumulation, and is associated with accelerated brain aging. This cross-sectional study examined how dietary iron intake and hemochromatosis-associated single nucleotide polymorphisms are associated with brain MRI phenotypes sensitive to iron. We used a subset of the UK Biobank (N=24,223 participants) to investigate associations between dietary heme and non-heme iron intake (dietary predictors), HFE SNPs rs1799945 and rs1800562 (genetic predictors), brain quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and T2* MRI phenotypes (primary outcomes) using multiple regression. We also investigated associations of HFE SNPs and dietary intake with hemoglobin, anemia risk, and MRI-derived liver iron levels as markers of systemic iron status. We compared brain QSM for rs1799945 and rs1800562 homozygotes and rs1799945/rs1800562 compound heterozygotes relative to control genotype subjects without either HFE SNP using ANCOVA and Tukey-Kramer post-hoc testing. Significance was set at false discovery rate (FDR) <0.05. Intake of dietary heme iron and both HFE SNPs were associated with increased QSM and decreased T2* MRI intensities (FDR<0.05), a pattern associated with increased brain iron levels. Non-heme iron intake was associated with a slight, but statistically significant, decrease in QSM and increase in T2* intensity, which is consistent with less brain iron. Both SNPs and heme iron intake were associated with higher hemoglobin and MRI-derived liver iron levels. Adjusted mean QSM intensity was generally highest for rs1800562 homozygotes and mostly higher in rs1799945 homozygotes and rs1799945/rs1800562 compound heterozygotes compared to control genotype. Dietary heme iron intake and SNPs linked to hemochromatosis are associated with altered brain MRI intensities consistent with elevated brain iron.

title: Responsive Neurostimulation of the Centromedian Nucleus of the Thalamus for the Treatment of Drug-Resistant Idiopathic Generalized Epilepsy: A Retrospective Analysis of Efficacy and Exploratory Role of Different Stimulation Frequency Paradigms.
abstract: Closed-loop (responsive) neurostimulation (RNS) targeting the bilateral centromedian thalamic nucleus (CMN) is a safe and efficacious therapy for idiopathic generalized epilepsy (IGE). However, the optimal stimulation parameters have yet to be elucidated. The aims of this study were to review the efficacy of CMN-RNS in drug-resistant IGE and discuss the potential role of stimulation frequency in CMN-RNS programming. This study is a single-institution retrospective analysis of 10 patients with drug-resistant IGE who underwent CMN-RNS implantation. Initial therapy programming consisted of bipolar settings with opposite polarity between burst 1/2 and initial current 0.5 mA, charge density 0.5 μC/cm2, frequency 125 Hz, pulse width 160 μsec, and burst duration 500 msec. If patients experienced seizures or developed paresthesia with increasing charge density, they were transitioned to mid (10-100 Hz) or low frequency (<10 Hz) stimulation. The mean age at surgery was 33 years, and mean epilepsy duration was 20 years prior to RNS implantation. Median post-implantation follow-up was 33.5 months. The median number of pre-implantation generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures per year was 5.5, and post-RNS was 2.5. Overall, there was a median 85.5% reduction in GTC frequency from the pre-RNS baseline. The median GTC-free interval was 16 months, and 40% of patients were GTC-free at last follow-up. The results of this cases series suggest CMN-RNS therapy in people with drug-resistant IGE may significantly reduce the frequency of GTC. Preliminary evidence may support alternative paradigms of mid and low-frequency stimulation when high-frequency stimulation is poorly tolerated or not efficacious.

title: A comparison of continuous-wave fNIRS with quantitative fMRI-derived indices of brain function in the visual cortex.
abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) both rely on the phenomenon of neurovascular coupling (NVC) to probe brain activity through their sensitivity to cerebral blood oxygenation. However, the relationship between fNIRS chromophores (oxy- and deoxyhaemoglobin, HbO and HbR), and fMRI (Blood Oxygen Level Dependent and Arterial Spin Labeling, BOLD and ASL) measurements, and whether this relationship remains consistent across subjects and physiological conditions, has only been partially characterised. We acquired concurrent continuous-wave fNIRS and gradient-echo (GE) and spin-echo (SE) BOLD-ASL fMRI in healthy adults (n = 10) during visual stimulation. By applying calibrated fMRI methodology, we examined the relationships between fNIRS-derived haemoglobin modulations and fMRI-derived modulations in macrovascular (GE-) and microvascular (SE-) BOLD signals, cerebral blood flow (CBF), and oxygen metabolism (CMRO₂). Group-level results showed strong temporal cross-modal agreement, with HbO and HbR tightly mirroring all fMRI signal time-courses (|r| > 0.8). A quantitative analysis of trial-by-trial modulations revealed distinct state-dependent behaviours: HbO maintained a stable relationship with the fMRI-derived metrics across conditions, whereas cross-modal relationships between HbR and fMRI-derived metrics substantially strengthened at higher flow-metabolism coupling (FMC), the ratio of CBF to CMRO₂ change, an index of the strength of NVC. Both HbO and HbR were more strongly associated with GE-BOLD than with SE-BOLD. These findings provide a rigorous physiological grounding for fNIRS signal interpretation, demonstrating its utility as a surrogate marker for specific haemodynamic and metabolic parameters.

title: Associations between autobiographical characteristics of past and future events, anhedonia and anticipatory pleasure: a cross-sectional study in a community sample of adolescents.
abstract: Impairments in autobiographical characteristics of Episodic Future Thinking (EFT) and Autobiographical (AM), such as reduced specificity, level of detail, and mental imagery, are associated with stress-related mental health problems in adults, including depression. The current study aims to identify which cognitive and emotional autobiographical characteristics, including objectively-rated level of specificity and autobiographical detail, predict unique variance in anhedonia and anticipatory pleasure in adolescents. Both are core symptoms of depression characterised by low positive affective experiences. By doing so, we aimed to identify modifiable cognitive processes that may improve the resilience of adolescents at an early stage before they develop psychopathology. An adolescent community sample (N = 149, M age = 13.21; SD = 1.04) completed self-report scales assessing anhedonia, resilience, and depressive symptoms, and the Episodic Future Thinking Test and Autobiographical Memory Test to measure EFT and AM variables. With respect to anhedonia, anticipated pleasure (EFT) accounted for unique variance. Regarding anticipatory pleasure, the findings consistently indicated that anticipated pleasure, mental imagery and level of detail (EFT) each served as unique predictors. Lower anhedonia levels fully mediated the positive relation between anticipated pleasure and resilience. Although findings should be interpreted considering the study limitations, clinical implications are discussed.

title: Ets2 Is an Activity-Dependent Transcriptional Regulator of a Fast-Twitch Muscle Program.
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
abstract: The functional properties of excitable cells, including skeletal muscle, are regulated by electrical activity. Distinct motoneuron firing patterns control contraction speed, strength, and endurance of fast- and slow-twitch myofibers by activating transcriptional programs that specify contractile and metabolic protein isoforms. Although transcriptional regulators of slow muscle adaptation are well characterized, less is known about activity-dependent mechanisms controlling expression of fast muscle genes. We previously showed that the quail fast troponin I (TnIf) intronic regulatory element (FIRE) is both necessary and sufficient for fast-muscle-specific transcription and responds selectively to brief, high-frequency (150 Hz) stimulation rather than to sustained low-frequency (20 Hz) activity. In this study, using mRNA microarray analysis of muscles subjected to different stimulation patterns, we identified E26 transformation-specific homolog 2 (Ets2) as a transcription factor rapidly and selectively induced by fast-patterned activity. Ets2 accumulates in nuclei of slow soleus muscle following fast, but not slow, stimulation, and it is expressed more abundantly in fast muscle. Ets2 binds a consensus Ets site within the TnIf FIRE, and mutation of this site abolishes enhancer activation by fast-patterned activity. Furthermore, Ets2 knockdown reduces transcription from both a trimerized Ets2-responsive reporter and a TnIf FIRE reporter specifically in fast muscles. To our knowledge, these findings identify Ets2 as the first transcription factor shown to selectively promote fast muscle gene expression in response to fast-patterned activity. Together with NFATc1, Ets2 may contribute to a dynamic regulatory mechanism that enables skeletal muscles to adapt their functional properties to changing physiological demands.

title: Exploring a Range of Potential Factors Promoting and Constraining EF in South African Preschoolers.
abstract: Socioeconomic disadvantage is widely associated with poorer cognitive and educational outcomes. However, emerging evidence suggests that children in low-income contexts may demonstrate resilience in executive function (EF) development. This study examined the predictors of EF in South African preschoolers from disadvantaged communities to identify modifiable, context-specific influences. 125 Children (aged 3-5 years) and their caregivers were recruited from 15 early childhood centers in Cape Town. Children completed three tablet-based EF tasks from the Early Years Toolbox measuring working memory, inhibition, shifting, while caregivers reported on demographic variables, household assets, child sleep, child screen time, child exposure to violence, and parenting practices. Multiple linear regressions examined predictors of child EF, with exploratory analyses on a subset (n = 22) for hair cortisol analysis. Older child age (β = 0.37, p < 0.001), caregiver secondary education (β = 0.22, p = 0.003), and fewer sleep difficulties (β = -0.45, p = 0.042) significantly predicted higher child EF scores, together explaining 25% of variance. Household assets, screen time, violence exposure, and parenting scores were non-significant. In the subsample, hair cortisol concentration correlated positively with EF (ρ = 0.55, p = 0.009), suggesting potential adaptive calibration under adversity. Findings highlight that modifiable proximal factors (e.g., caregiver education and child sleep) shape EF development more strongly than socioeconomic indicators. Results challenge the presumed universality of SES-EF gradients and underscore the importance of culturally grounded, contextually validated measures for understanding resilience and early cognitive development in Majority World settings.

title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry in Neurobiology: From Imaging to Proteomics.
journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has emerged as a versatile approach for probing molecules with high selectivity and minimal perturbation. While applicable to diverse biomolecules, its use in protein studies has proven particularly powerful, especially in neurobiology, where precise molecular tools are essential. A key technology enabling such precision is genetic code expansion (GCE), which allows the incorporation of unnatural amino acids (UAAs) bearing bioorthogonal handles into proteins. These UAAs can be introduced site-specifically to label defined proteins or proteome-wide for systems-level analysis. Complementing this, proteome-wide labeling can be achieved through metabolic incorporation of amino acid analogs. Coupled with copper-catalyzed or strain-promoted click reactions, these labeling technologies enable applications ranging from protein visualization to mass spectrometry-based proteomics. Ongoing advances in UAA incorporation strategies and the chemical diversity of available UAAs continue to broaden the opportunities to study protein expression, localization, and dynamics.
